source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Heater and Air Conditioning, p.1A-11

procedures.title: Four-Season air conditioning controls: Corvette
steps: Maximum heat: set the left indicator to 'hot', the right indicator to 'Htr' and the fan to 'Hi'.
Maximum cooling: set the left indicator to 'cold', the right indicator to 'A/C' and the fan to 'Hi'.
De-ice: set the left indicator to 'hot', the right indicator to 'de-ice' and the fan to 'Hi'.
notes: Controls are a new thumb-wheel design in the floor console (see figure 16 in the manual); airflow is basically as on the other car lines (figure 14).
Fan lever (front of panel): moving it left to right runs the three-speed blower.
Left thumb-wheel (air source and temperature): 'off' shuts down the whole system; 'vent' detent puts the vacuum-operated air selector doors on outside air.

At the 'cold' detent: selector doors go to recirculated air, the temperature door goes to cold, the blower runs on low automatically, and the compressor runs if the ambient temperature is above 30°F and/or the right indicator is on the 'A/C' side of the 'Htr' detent.
Moving past 'cold' opens the vacuum-operated heater water shut-off valve and the temperature door to reach the chosen temperature.

Right thumb-wheel (outlets/defroster): 'A/C' sends all air through the dash outlets via the vacuum-operated outlets door; the dot detent between 'A/C' and 'HTR' gives bi-level (dash and floor) flow; 'Htr' sends all air to the floor outlet and stops the compressor; between 'HTR' and 'De-ice' the cable-operated defroster door sends part or all of the air to the defroster outlets.
Results can be moderated with the fan speed or by moving the temperature indicator between 'hot' and 'cold'.
